title: L&T lands a $1.57B order to build India's largest B300 AI factory for Together AI
subtitle: The Chennai buildout is a 10,000-GPU first phase on a gigawatt-scale site — and the biggest single Indian AI-infrastructure deal to date.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Larsen & Toubro said on August 13 that its subsidiary Vyoma.AI will build a 10,000-GPU Nvidia B300 AI factory at its Chennai data-centre campus for San Francisco-based Together AI. The order is worth up to ₹15,000 crore, roughly $1.57 billion. The campus is designed for gigawatt-scale over time, with the first phase sized at 250 megawatts of power. Together AI, last valued at about $8.3 billion in July, will operate the site as an AI-native cloud for training, fine-tuning, and large-scale inference.

The mechanism worth noticing is where the compute is going. Together AI does not train frontier models — it rents GPUs and open-model inference to other companies that do. A 10,000-B300 cluster in India therefore functions as neutral capacity, sold by the hour to whichever labs and enterprises need it, with no allegiance to any single foundation-model provider. That is a different shape from the Anthropic–Google–Broadcom or OpenAI–Nvidia mega-deals of the last two months, which are locked to one buyer's roadmap.

It also lands in a country the current export-control regime treats as friendly. The B300 is the same silicon the Commerce Department has been rationing to Chinese firms; India can buy it on standard commercial terms, and L&T has been racking up orders from Nvidia-adjacent buyers on the strength of that fact. Chennai now joins Bengaluru and Hyderabad as sites where the AI infrastructure buildout has crossed the gigawatt threshold, and India is quietly becoming one of the three or four places outside the US where frontier-scale training can be run at all.

Takeaway for learners: infrastructure is a career track. Every headline this year has been about model releases, but the labs that ship those models rent their compute from a small number of hyperscalers and neutral clouds — and those companies are hiring at a pace the labs cannot match. If you have a systems, networking, or datacenter-operations background and you have been eyeing the AI wave from the outside, the AI-cloud layer is where the biggest gap between demand and supply sits.
